editorial.headline: The Work Behind a Game’s Content
editorial.standfirst: Game content design shapes mechanics, stories, visual worlds, interfaces and levels; it is nationally open to full foreign ownership at every scale, yet PMA registration is blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
Game content design is the disciplined planning work that gives a game its playable and expressive shape. Under this activity, it includes devising game-mechanics logic and story, directing the artistic design of characters, visual interfaces and levels, and resolving technical design connected with the technology used. It also includes preparing design documents, conducting research and development, and carrying out other supporting activity. The focus is the creative and technical blueprint: the connected decisions through which a game’s content is conceived, articulated and developed. Its components run from play logic and narrative through visual and technical decisions to the documents and research that support them.

Registration is open to businesses at micro, small, medium and large scale. Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment and permits a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. No separate scale is excluded in the record: each of the four stated scales is open. The range of listed work explains the breadth of that national position: a business may work across narrative planning, mechanics, artistic direction, interface and level design, technical design, documentation and research, rather than being confined to one creative discipline. The scope holds these strands together as content-design activity.

Bali alters the immediate conclusion. A foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. At the large scale, every scope within the activity is classified by OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium applies to the Low and Medium-Low risk classifications recorded here; this activity is therefore blocked for PMA registration. The moratorium identified in the record dates from the thirteenth of May, two thousand and twenty-six. It is not a narrower condition attached to a single design element: every scope is in those risk classes at the large scale.

The distinction is decisive rather than technical. The national record addresses foreign ownership and allows the full 100% ceiling; the Bali rule addresses whether PMA registration is available in the province. For founders, the result is a clean split: every listed business scale is nationally open, yet Bali does not presently provide a PMA registration route for this activity. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not make PMA registration available in Bali. The record gives the local registration block its own rule.
